content:
I wanted to share my hobby project, Monad, which is an early stage dependently typed functional language that compiles to LLVM.

I developed the first Rust interpreter by hand and I gradually started to use more LLMs since it meant I could do more with higher quality and spend more time on design and experimentation. I consider the move to using AI agents for coding is similar to the introduction of compilers rather than writing assembly.

I wanted to have something that could be as performant and safe as Rust, but with the ergonomics, verifiability power and expressiveness of languages like Haskell, Lean, ATS or Idris. That is quite ambitious so I might not succeed.

The type system is currently immature and has not been in focus. I will work more on adding full support for something in the line of Caclulus of Inductive Constructions and perhaps even Univalence support. This has not been fully settled yet as the focus is still on getting a working practical language landed before anneling the types and language. The core language will also not support tactics or any proof tooling outside of representing the raw type structure.

A simple hello world example is quite similar to Lean:

def main : IO Unit := println "Hello World!"

The latest milestone is that it can now compile itself and is therefore self hosted. The documentation is a bit outdated, but I will update it soon.

https://github.com/monad-lang/monad

https://monad-lang.org

There is still a lot to be done.

If you are interested in discussing more and following development come over to the Zulip https://monad-lang.zulipchat.com.

I am looking for and happy for bug-reports, feedback and criticism, but not PRs and new contributions just yet.
What's the unique selling point of this language? Lean4 can already do monads, and Idris2 has QTT as well. (sorry if rough question).

It is still in heavy development, but Monad is intended to bring the performance of languages like Rust and ATS into an ergonomic, verifiably safe and dependently typed language. So you can write low level code with provable invariants.
Although this is not finished implementation.
One goal is to make dependent types and monadic conputation more available main stream practical programming.
It is a lot simpler in design than Lean4. Idris2 is also a huge inspiration, but I have taken some different choices.
I am also considering supporting univalence in the type system which as far as I know only lean2 supported for a short while.
MOnad is Not A Digital proof assistant (Monad) also.
Do you have an example where the Rust-like performance will materialize, i.e. where it might be on the same level as Rust and/or Lean in the future?
In the future hopefully in most applications. Monad compiles to LLVM just like Rust. It is currently Garbage collected, but that will be removed when the QTT implementation and more stabilizes.
I mean how will Monad achieve it, not where will it be applicable. Sorry, I should have been clearer.

That is a longer question. I am trying out a combination of ideas from Idris, Rust and ATS. By keeping track of shared memory and pointers during compile time we can verifiably insert free(ptr) when a memory is no longer needed and also do in place mutations to recycle memory like Lean does. Essentially a sort of compile time reference counting.
But this is all very experimental currently.
Also being optimized for safe and verifiable LLM assisted code generation is also a goal.
